body:
The source-store metadata limit now uses the same pretty-JSON serializer with a
byte counter instead of retaining a temporary output buffer. The exact 64-KiB
boundary, parsing/error order, original byte versions and canonical durable source
bytes remain. Three release comparisons show 1.4–3.2 ms median gains for 1,000 rich
cards. Small contexts are unchanged; ordinary/long-body gains are below 1 ms
outside an unrepeated control outlier. All 800 selected context reads preserve
full normalized output and current identity/version/budget checks. Isolated
serializer comparisons check 240,000 exact lengths; these are not UI/RSS claims.

Nine document regressions and the 468-test full gate pass. Normally paired
Chromium/WebKit protocol and all 14 editor scenarios pass in both engines. The
existing HTTPS application is rebuilt/restarted, preserving 77 prior versions,
three pins, preferences, certificate, instance/epoch and complete native CLI
context; all 32 served assets match the rebuilt frontend. Both owner card changes
remain separate. Broader performance, Linux widget/QML, physical iPhone and release
acceptance remain open. Next measure duplicate-key map lookups without changing
rejection order. See progress/2026-10-01-source-metadata-budget.md.

metadata.summary: Count canonical metadata bytes without retaining a temporary buffer
